basis: Dyskeratosis congenita is defined by nail/skin abnormalities, oral leukoplakia and marrow failure; pulmonary fibrosis is variable and not established at >=30% for this subtype.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Histidine metabolism defect; intellectual disability and cerebellar dysfunction in reported cases, with dysarthria annotated 80-99%; evidence comes from very few patients.
Malignant tumour arising in the external, middle or inner ear; other organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella.
Inherited susceptibility to febrile seizures; fever does not establish an infectious mechanism.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and metastatic sites are not inherent to this concept.
Glycosylation disorder; intellectual disability 9/15 and motor delay 9/13 support neurologic involvement. Osteoarthritis and muscle hypertrophy each occur in 4/15, below 30%.
Oral burning syndrome classified as a mouth disorder; psychiatric associations do not add an axis, and a separate neurologic lesion is not established.
Monogenic diabetes affecting insulin secretion; diabetic organ complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Lymphoid malignancy arising in orbital structures; lymphoma supplies the haematologic and infectious_immune mechanisms.
Eosinophil-mediated pulmonary inflammation causing acute respiratory failure; tissue eosinophilia does not establish a separate blood-cell disorder.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability.
Oral blisters and GI inflammation occur in 30-79%; urinary abnormalities are nonspecific, while documented urethral strictures occur in only 5-29%, so renal is omitted.
Developmental pilosebaceous skin lesions; ocular, neurologic and skeletal abnormalities are each annotated only 5-29%.
Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; neurodevelopmental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting hypoglycemic neurologic injury. Cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.
Contractures 5/12 and muscle-fiber abnormalities 3/5 support musculoskeletal damage; visual impairment and ventilatory failure may be neurologic without direct eye or lung lesions.
Acquired transmissible prion disease causing progressive brain degeneration; lymphoid prion carriage does not establish blood-organ dysfunction.
Inherited distal motor neuron degeneration; muscle weakness and wasting are neurogenic rather than evidence of a primary muscle disorder.
Open spinal dysraphism combining split-cord malformation and hemicord myeloschisis, within the spina bifida aperta spectrum.
Urea-cycle disorder; hyperammonemic encephalopathy with ataxia and impaired consciousness is a defining symptomatic presentation. Scotomas alone do not establish ocular damage.
Defined by growth hormone deficiency and congenital antibody deficiency; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
HPO annotates bleeding/coagulopathy, pyloric stenosis and scoliosis at 80-99%; cardiac defects at 30-79% omitted at cap. Frequencies may overrepresent syndromic forms.
Sclerosing bone dysplasia; supplied HPO annotates cranial nerve paralysis at 80-99%, supporting neurologic damage, although this frequency is atypical clinically.
Defined by brief afebrile seizures during mild gastroenteritis; gastroenteritis is the associated triggering illness, with no CNS infection or persistent additional organ damage.
Congenital fusion of the jaws with cleft palate defines skeletal and oral structural involvement.
